newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hochtief nudged higher by Keitel interview.
newsitem.headline: Hochtief nudged higher by Keitel interview.

text.p: Shares in German construction group Hochtief AG rose on Monday after an interview with its management board chairman Hans-Peter Keitel in which he affirmed the group was seeking to gain more of its revenues in civil engineering projects.

Hochtief stock rose 1.90 marks ($1.14) to 70.80 as analysts said such a move, which Hochtief has for some time been signalling, was seen positively because of the higher margins available for such work compared to standard construction projects.

"It is correct to say that construction will play a smaller role for us in future and that projects such as the Duesseldorf and Berlin airports will have a significantly greater one," Keitel said in the interview.
He said that Hochtief would be among the interested parties due to hold talks with regional authorities on the details of the privatisation of the Duesseldorf airport in the coming days.
He added that in Hochtief's case, the crucial factor affecting its involvement was not the size of the stake it ended up with but the extent of management control on offer.

Keitel also referred to the problem of fierce price competition in the German construction market, saying that existing cost-cutting measures would have to be continued this year, at an albeit slower pace.
